title: Ship React Native updates with CodePush
tagline: Push a new JavaScript bundle to installed apps without a store review.
intro: CodePush swaps the JavaScript bundle inside an installed app. Native code still needs a store release; everything written in JS does not.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Set up once, then every release is one command.

blocks.caption: From your terminal to a phone that already has the app.

items.label: Install the CLI
items.detail: appcenter-cli logs you in and is the tool every later step runs through
explain: npm install -g appcenter-cli installs it globally. The older code-push-cli is deprecated, so do not start a project on it.
appcenter login opens a browser and hands back a token; pasting it into the terminal ties the CLI to your account.

items.label: Create the app
items.detail: One App Center app per platform: iOS and Android get separate deployment keys
explain: appcenter apps create -d demo -o iOS -p React-Native creates the iOS half; run it again with -o Android for the other.
-d is the display name, -o the operating system and -p the platform. The app then shows up on the App Center home page.

items.label: Wire the SDK
items.detail: react-native-code-push makes the release build read its bundle from CodePush
explain: On iOS, sourceURLForBridge returns [CodePush bundleURL] in release and keeps the Metro URL in debug, so development is untouched.
The deployment key goes into Info.plist as CodePushDeploymentKey. Staging and Production each have one, and the key decides which channel a build listens to.
Wrapping the root component with codePush() is what makes the app check for an update when it starts.

items.label: Release
items.detail: release-react bundles the JS and uploads it to one deployment, Staging or Production
explain: appcenter codepush release-react -a damhongduc/demo -d Staging: -a is owner/app and -d is the deployment to publish into.
Each release gets a label such as v3 on the CodePush page, which is how you tell which bundle a device is running.

items.label: Device updates
items.detail: A release build checks on launch, downloads the bundle and applies it on the next start
explain: Test it with npx react-native run-ios --configuration Release — a debug build reads Metro and never asks CodePush.
The default policy installs on the next restart, so kill and reopen the app after a release to see the change.

body: Microsoft retired App Center on 31 March 2025. Existing CodePush setups need the self-hosted CodePush server Microsoft open-sourced, or another OTA service.
The client-side steps below stay the same either way; only the server the CLI talks to changes.

sections.title: Install the CLI and log in

blocks.caption: The login prints a token in the browser; paste it back into the terminal
One app per platform
code: appcenter apps create -d demo -o iOS -p React-Native
appcenter apps create -d demo -o Android -p React-Native

sections.title: Install the SDK on iOS
sections.summary: Four edits, all in the native project.

items: Open AppDelegate.m and add #import <CodePush/CodePush.h> at the top.
Replace the release branch of sourceURLForBridge with [CodePush bundleURL].
In App Center, open Distribute → CodePush → Create standard deployment, then copy the keys from the settings icon.
Add CodePushDeploymentKey to Info.plist with the Staging or Production key.
Wrap the root component: export default codePush(App).

blocks.caption: Debug still reads Metro; only release asks CodePush
-a is owner/app, -d is Staging or Production

rows: Owner and app name, as owner/app

sections.title: See it land
sections.summary: A release build, a change, a restart.

items: Run the app in release mode: npx react-native run-ios --configuration Release
Change something visible, such as a background colour or a label
Release it to the deployment whose key is in Info.plist
Wait a few minutes, then close and reopen the app

body: Only JavaScript and assets travel through CodePush. A new native module or a changed Podfile still needs a store build.
